problem_statement: The Codrops Astro Shop demo (view transitions between a product grid and product detail pages) shows its four shirts — 705 Brave, Haryo Setyadi, Faith Yarn T-Shirt, and T-Shirt 705 — as one flat gallery on the index with no way to shop by collection. Turn the product grid into a real 'Shop the collection' filter: a chip row (All / Everyday / Statement / Under $100, derived from the existing product prices) above the product cards that re-renders the visible cards and updates a live 'Showing N of 4 shirts · <Collection>' result count. Reuse the same collection filter as a compact rail above the 'You might also like' recommendations on the product detail page, so the collection context follows the shopper across the list-to-detail view transition. Keep the minimalist Codrops shop language (white cards, gray-200 borders, rounded-2xl corners, restrained black CTAs on the gray-50 ground), the product images, names, prices, view-transition names, the breadcrumb, and the Add to cart button. The chip row and product grid must wrap cleanly at 390px with no horizontal overflow, the active chip must stay legible, the cards must keep stable non-overlapping dimensions, and clicking a collection chip must actually filter the cards and update the count.
required_content: The index product grid becomes a 'Shop the collection' filter: an All / Everyday / Statement / Under $100 chip row over the four product cards with a live 'Showing N of 4 shirts' result count derived from the existing product data.
Clicking a collection chip re-renders the visible product cards and updates the count readout so it matches the cards shown (e.g. 'Showing 2 of 4 shirts · Everyday').
The same collection filter appears as a compact rail above the product detail 'You might also like' recommendations, so the collection context carries across the list-to-detail view transition.
The product cards, product images, product names, prices, view-transition names, breadcrumb, and Add to cart button remain unchanged.
The active collection chip stays legible and the product cards keep stable, non-overlapping dimensions consistent with the existing card treatment.
The collection chip row and product grid have no horizontal overflow, clipped cards, or overlapping text on the 390px mobile index and product-detail states.
design_constraints: Preserve the minimalist Codrops/Astro shop visual language: white cards, gray-200 borders, rounded-2xl corners, compact metadata, and restrained black CTAs on the gray-50 ground; the active filter chip fills solid near-black with white text.
Do not convert the shop into a bright SaaS landing page, a dashboard, or a card-heavy marketing site; it must stay a minimal editorial product demo.
Build the collection filter from the existing four products and their real prices; do not introduce external assets or a new catalog.
Keep the view-transition product image/title/description/price naming intact so route transitions still work, and keep the breadcrumb, Add to cart button, and recommendations available.
Product cards must keep restrained density, stable dimensions, readable metadata, and consistent border/radius treatment; the active filter chip must have legible contrast.
The collection chip row and product grid must remain responsive with no horizontal overflow at 390px on the index and the product detail page.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial, and mobile_initial show the 'Shop the collection' filter chip row and all four product cards.
desktop_product_detail and mobile_product_detail show Haryo Setyadi, the price, Add to cart, the breadcrumb Back to collection affordance, and the collection filter rail above the recommendations.
desktop_recommendations shows the same-collection 'You might also like' recommendations with the collection filter rail above them.
desktop_collection_everyday shows the index after clicking the Everyday collection chip: the grid re-filters and the count readout updates to 'Showing 2 of 4 shirts · Everyday'.
mobile_initial and mobile_product_detail must have no horizontal overflow (the reference wraps the chip row; the original-with-defect baseline overflows).

change_completion: The index grid is a working 'Shop the collection' filter with an All / Everyday / Statement / Under $100 chip row and a live 'Showing N of 4 shirts' count.
Clicking a collection chip filters the visible product cards and updates the count so it matches the cards actually shown.
The collection filter is reused as a compact rail above the product detail recommendations for a continuous cross-page collection context.
The product images, names, prices, view-transition names, breadcrumb, and Add to cart button remain available.
design_consistency: The collection filter matches the minimal Codrops shop system: white cards, gray borders, rounded corners, restrained black CTAs, and compact metadata.
The active collection chip is legible and the product cards keep stable, non-overlapping dimensions.
The shop stays a minimal editorial product demo rather than a generic dashboard.
regression: The four products, their images, prices, view-transition names, breadcrumb, Add to cart button, and recommendations are not removed.
External tutorial/GitHub links still open externally and the product detail route stays consistent.
responsive: Mobile index and product-detail states have no horizontal overflow and keep the product cards reachable.
The collection chip row and product cards wrap cleanly at 390px width.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Astro modify/cross_page task on the Codrops astro-shop-view-transitions demo. The native commerce lever is the product grid's own 'Shop the collection' filter — a chip row (All / Everyday / Statement / Under $100, derived from the products' own prices) that re-renders the product cards and updates a live result count, reused as a compact rail above the product-detail recommendations for cross-page continuity. Runability passes with npm install and a static astro build served from dist. Captures show a minimal white-card shop with real product photography, the filterable collection grid, and the product detail view transition.
